prompt: The shop's repository was created in `us-central1` by mistake, and the services run in São Paulo. What does fixing it take?
hint: Which properties of a repository can change after it is created?

choices.text: Updating the repository's location with gcloud
choices.why: The location is fixed at creation; there is no command that moves it.

choices.text: A new repository, a copy, and every deployment changed
choices.why: Right. The region is part of the address, so the address changes with it.

choices.text: Nothing: images are global once pushed
choices.why: A repository lives in one location, and pulls from elsewhere pay for the transfer.

choices.text: Renaming the repository to include the region
choices.why: The name is fixed too, and a name is not a location.

prompt: Builds fail now and then because Docker Hub refuses anonymous pulls of the base image. Which kind of repository addresses that inside your project?
hint: A cache in front of another registry.

choices.text: A standard repository
choices.why: A standard one stores what you push; it fetches nothing from Docker Hub.

choices.text: A virtual repository
choices.why: A virtual one fronts other repositories you already have; it caches nothing itself.

choices.text: A remote one
choices.why: Right. Only the first pull of each image goes to Docker Hub; the rest come from your cache.

choices.text: A repository in a multi-region such as us
choices.why: A multi-region changes where images are stored, not where they come from.

prompt: The API's runtime account was given `roles/artifactregistry.reader` on the project rather than on `shop`. What does that allow that it should not?
hint: A role on a parent applies to everything under it.

choices.text: Pushing images to shop
choices.why: Reader never pushes, wherever it is granted.

choices.text: Deleting the repository
choices.why: Deletion needs an admin role, not reader.

choices.text: Pulling every image in every repository of the project
choices.why: Right. Including other teams' images, which carry their code.

choices.text: Nothing more: reader on the project and on the repository are the same
choices.why: They differ in reach: one repository against all of them.

prompt: You push a new build under the tag `v1`, which already pointed at an older image. What does a registry without immutable tags do?
hint: Look at the two digests in the transcript.

choices.text: Refuses the push
choices.why: Only an immutable-tags repository refuses; the local one accepted it.

choices.text: Moves v1 to the new image, silently
choices.why: Right. One tag, a new digest, and no message.

choices.text: Keeps both images under v1 and serves the older one
choices.why: A tag points at exactly one image at a time.

choices.text: Renames the old image to v1-1 and gives the new one v1
choices.why: No registry invents tags; the old image is simply left untagged.

prompt: After the second push of `v1`, can the first image still be run?
hint: The tag left it. Is it deleted?

choices.text: No: the push replaced it in the registry
choices.why: Pushing moves a tag; it deletes no image.

choices.text: Only from the machine that built it, out of its local cache
choices.why: The transcript removed the local copy and pulled it back from the registry.

choices.text: Yes, by pulling v1 with --previous
choices.why: There is no such option; the tag knows only where it points now.

choices.text: Yes, by its digest, until something deletes it
choices.why: Right. It is untagged, which is what a cleanup policy looks for.

prompt: A Compute Engine machine's startup script runs `docker run …/shop/api:latest`. It reboots after a push to `latest`. What does it run?
hint: Who resolved the tag, and when?

choices.text: The new image, whatever latest points at when it pulls
choices.why: Right. Nothing recorded a digest, so the reboot is a deploy nobody chose.

choices.text: The image it ran before the reboot, which Docker remembers
choices.why: docker run with a tag pulls only if missing; with a fresh pull policy, it gets the new one. The script did not pin anything.

choices.text: The image from the revision, as Cloud Run does
choices.why: Revisions are Cloud Run's; a startup script has none.

choices.text: Nothing: Docker refuses latest on a server
choices.why: latest is an ordinary tag; nothing refuses it.

prompt: Match each place to what it should name.
hint: A person reads one, a machine runs the other.

prompt: Immutable tags are turned on for `shop`. The build still pushes `:latest` after `:$SHORT_SHA`. What happens on the second build?
hint: Which tags does the setting cover?

choices.text: It succeeds: latest is exempt
choices.why: No tag is exempt, latest included.

choices.text: The push of latest is refused
choices.why: Right. Moving latest is moving a tag, which the repository now refuses.

choices.text: Both pushes are refused, because the image already exists
choices.why: The commit tag is new each time, so it is accepted.

choices.text: latest is moved and a warning is logged in Cloud Logging
choices.why: Immutability refuses; it does not warn and move anyway.

prompt: A cleanup policy deletes tagged images older than 90 days, with no `Keep` rule. The API has run one image for four months without a deploy. What is the risk?
hint: Does a policy know what is running?

choices.text: None: a running image is never deleted
choices.why: The policy knows tags and ages, not deployments.

choices.text: The running container stops at once
choices.why: A running container keeps its copy; the failure waits for the next pull.

choices.text: The image is deleted and the next restart cannot pull it
choices.why: Right. Which is why the shop keeps its last ten versions.

choices.text: The policy refuses to run until a Keep rule exists
choices.why: Nothing requires a Keep rule; that is the author's job.

prompt: A repository holds 60.5 GiB all month. At 0.10 USD per GiB-month after the first 0.5 GiB free, what is the month's storage bill?
hint: Subtract the free half gibibyte first.

prompt: The flag that makes `set-cleanup-policies` report what it would delete, deleting nothing, is `--___`.
hint: Two words joined by a hyphen.

prompt: An image was clean when it was pushed on Monday. On Thursday it shows a critical finding, and nobody touched it. Why?
hint: Scanning keeps going after the push.

choices.text: Somebody pushed over its digest
choices.why: A digest cannot point at another image.

choices.text: A new advisory was published, and the image was re-scanned
choices.why: Right. For 30 days the findings follow the advisories, not the image.

choices.text: The first scan had not finished
choices.why: Monday's result was complete; Thursday's is about a newer advisory.

choices.text: Scanning runs the image and found the flaw at run time
choices.why: Artifact Analysis reads package versions; it never runs the image.

prompt: Which finding does the shop act on first?
hint: Something you can do, in something that runs.

choices.text: A critical CVE with no fixed version, in an image nobody deploys
choices.why: No fix and no running copy: there is nothing to do and nothing at stake yet.

choices.text: The finding with the highest CVSS score
choices.why: The effective severity for the distribution says more, and a fix matters as much.

choices.text: A high finding with a fixed version, in the image the API runs
choices.why: Right. A fix exists and it matters; usually a newer base image.

choices.text: A low finding in app.py
choices.why: Scanning reads packages, not your own source file.

prompt: At 0.26 USD per scan, what do 200 pushes a month cost in scanning?
A team wants scanning to stop a vulnerable image from reaching production. What is missing if they only turn scanning on?

choices.text: A remote repository in front of Docker Hub
choices.why: That is about where base images come from, not about refusing a deployment.

choices.text: Immutable tags
choices.why: They stop tags moving; a vulnerable image with a fresh tag is accepted.

choices.text: A check at deploy time that refuses it
choices.why: Right. Scanning reports; lesson 4's admission policy is what refuses.

choices.text: Nothing: a critical finding blocks pulls of the image
choices.why: Findings block nothing; the image pulls as before.
